name: Josuke and Complete Graph
description: Josuke received a huge undirected weighted complete$$$^\dagger$$$ graph $$$G$$$ as a gift from his grandfather. The graph contains $$$10^{18}$$$ vertices. The peculiarity of the gift is that the weight of the edge between the different vertices $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ is equal to $$$\gcd(u, v)^\ddagger$$$. Josuke decided to experiment and make a new graph $$$G'$$$. To do this, he chooses two integers $$$l \le r$$$ and deletes all vertices except such vertices $$$v$$$ that $$$l \le v \le r$$$, and also deletes all the edges except between the remaining vertices. Now Josuke is wondering how many different weights are there in $$$G'$$$. Since their count turned out to be huge, he asks for your help. $$$^\dagger$$$ A complete graph is a simple undirected graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is adjacent. $$$^\ddagger$$$ $$$\gcd(x, y)$$$ denotes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the numbers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 100$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains two numbers $$$l$$$, $$$r$$$ ($$$1 \le l \le r \le 10^{18}$$$, $$$l \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: For each test case print a single number — the number of different weights among the remaining edges.
approach_summary: Apply Euclidean Algorithm paradigm under the Number Theory framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
